pressure.title: High temperature and pressure dissolve the alumina
pressure.description: In digestion hot caustic liquor dissolves the alumina minerals: Al(OH)₃ + NaOH → NaAl(OH)₄. Gibbsitic bauxite digests at about 140–150 °C; boehmitic/diaspore bauxites need ~ 230–270 °C, which means pressures up to roughly 30–35 bar. Vessels in series give the residence time needed while keeping the slurry hot and well mixed.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Autoclave — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Digestion Autoclave.
Digestion autoclaves are agitated pressure vessels in series where hot caustic liquor dissolves alumina from bauxite (Al(OH)₃ + NaOH → NaAl(OH)₄).
Live steam injection heats the slurry to digestion temperature and the series of vessels provides the residence time.
Typical applications include high-temperature digestion of boehmitic/diasporic bauxite; low-temperature (gibbsitic) digesters at atmospheric-to-moderate pressure.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Autoclave 1: Agitator Shaft & Impellers, Autoclave 2: Agitator Shaft & Impellers, Autoclave 3: Agitator Shaft & Impellers.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Autoclave — Operation

script.narration: How the Digestion Autoclave works.
Preheated slurry enters autoclave 1.
Live steam heats it to digestion temperature.
Agitators keep solids suspended.
Slurry overflows through the series.
Digested slurry leaves to flash cooling.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
In digestion hot caustic liquor dissolves the alumina minerals: Al(OH)₃ + NaOH → NaAl(OH)₄.

video_tutorials.title: Digestion Autoclave — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Digestion Autoclave.
Monitor temperature, pressure, agitator load.
Thickness checks at erosion points.
Descale vessels; inspect agitators.
Watch for scaling: lower volume, heat transfer. Common cause: DSP/titanate.
Watch for erosion leaks: leaks at transfer lines. Common cause: high velocity slurry.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
